The backend application is built using FastAPI (Python) following a modular, layered architecture. Each domain entity is organized into separate Model, Schema, Router, and Service layers as designed in Form 3.
The core module provides foundational services used across the entire backend:
– Centralized configuration using Pydantic BaseSettings. Reads DATABASE_URL, SECRET_KEY, ALGORITHM (default HS256), and ACCESS_TOKEN_EXPIRE_MINUTES from environment variables via .env file.
– Creates the SQLAlchemy engine connected to Supabase PostgreSQL. Provides SessionLocal factory and get_db() dependency for automatic session lifecycle management per HTTP request.

– Handles two security functions: (1) Password hashing using bcrypt via passlib with hash_password() and verify_password() functions, and (2) JWT token management using python-jose with create_access_token() and decode_access_token(). Tokens carry sub (user UUID), role, and exp claims using HS256 algorithm.

– Implements FastAPI injectable dependency guards for authentication and RBAC. get_current_user() decodes the JWT Bearer token and fetches the User from the database. require_role(*roles) is a factory function that returns a guard raising HTTP 403 if the user's role is not in the allowed set. Shortcut guards: get_current_admin, get_current_manager, get_current_finance, get_current_admin_or_manager.

– DEPRECATED backward-compatibility shim. This file only re-exports all SQLAlchemy models (User, Asset, AssetRequest, Transaction, Invoice, Incident, HandoverToken, UserBehaviorStats) from app/models/ and emits a DeprecationWarning advising to import directly from app.models instead. Kept temporarily to avoid breaking older import paths; will be removed in a future release.
All SQLAlchemy ORM models map to Supabase PostgreSQL tables. Each entity resides in its own file:

UUID PK, employee_id, email, role, department, clearance_level (1-5), employment_status, hire_date, risk_score (0-100), risk_score_tier, password_hash, public_key (Ed25519, nullable), last_login_at, timestamps. Relationships: requests, behavior_stats (1:1), invoices, incidents_reported.
BigInt PK, asset_code, asset_name, category, model, serial_number, purchase_value, location, current_condition, status, notes, timestamps. Relationships: requests, transactions, incidents.

BigInt PK, request_code (REQ-YYYY-NNNN), user_id (FK→users), asset_id (FK→assets), reason, requested_start/end dates, risk_score_snapshot, risk_tier_snapshot, ai_decision_reason, status (7 states: pending_admin, pending_manager, approved, rejected, handed_over, returned, cancelled), approved_by (FK→users), rejection_reason, timestamps.

BigInt PK, transaction_code (TXN-YYYY-NNNN), request_id, asset_id, borrower_id, admin_id, action (6 types), payload (JSONB), previous_hash (SHA-256), current_hash (SHA-256), signature (Ed25519), status, occurred_at. Append-only: enforced via database trigger preventing UPDATE/DELETE.

BigInt PK, invoice_code (INV-YYYY-NNNN), transaction_id, user_id, fine_amount, reason, status (unpaid/paid/verified/cancelled), payment_method, payment_proof_url, paid_at, verified_by, due_date, timestamps.

BigInt PK, incident_code (INC-YYYY-NNNN), reporter_id, asset_id, description, severity (low/medium/severe/lost/critical), status (open/investigating/resolved/closed), resolved_by, resolution_notes, timestamps.
BigInt PK, token (128 chars), request_id, issued_by, signature (Ed25519), issued_at, expires_at, scanned_at, scanned_by, status (active/used/expired/revoked).

user_id (UUID PK, FK→users), total_borrows, total_returns, on_time_returns, late_returns, damage_count, lost_count, total_fines, unpaid_fines, last_calculated_at. 1:1 relationship with User. Serves as denormalized feature store for AI risk scoring.
Pydantic v2 schemas handle request validation, response serialization, and enum definitions. Each entity has Create, Update, and Response schemas. Key file:

– Defines all system enums: UserRole (user/admin/manager/finance), EmploymentStatus, RiskTier (Low/Medium/High/Critical), AssetCategory, AssetCondition (good/fair/damaged/lost), AssetStatus (available/borrowed/maintenance/retired), RequestStatus (7 states), TransactionAction (borrow/return/damage_report/lost_report/fine_issued/handover), TransactionStatus, InvoiceStatus, PaymentMethod, IncidentSeverity, IncidentStatus, TokenStatus.
Eight routers handle all API endpoints under the /api/v1/ prefix:
POST /login (OAuth2 form-encoded, returns JWT + user profile), GET /me (current user), POST /logout
CRUD: GET / (list all), GET /{id}, POST / (admin only), PATCH /{id} (admin only), DELETE /{id} (admin only)
GET /me, CRUD for admin: GET /, GET /{id}, POST / (auto-hashes password, creates behavior_stats), PATCH /{id}, DELETE /{id}

POST / (user creates request, AI risk routing snapshots user risk_score and routes to pending_admin or pending_manager), GET /, GET /{id}, PATCH /{id}/approve (admin/manager), PATCH /{id}/reject, PATCH /{id}/return (admin, with condition assessment, auto-generates fine invoice if damaged/late)
GET /, GET /{id}, POST / (creates ledger entry with chained hash fields), GET /verify/ledger (integrity verification stub)
POST / (any auth, auto-generates incident code), GET /, GET /{id}, PATCH /{id} (admin/manager can update status/resolution), DELETE /{id} (admin only)
GET /, GET /{id}, POST / (finance/admin), PATCH /{id} (finance/admin), PATCH /{id}/verify-payment (finance only, verifies payment proof)
POST /generate (admin generates QR token for approved request), POST /scan (user scans token to confirm receipt), GET /{id}/verify (admin verifies token authenticity), GET /, GET /{id}

It only re-exports Asset schemas (AssetBase, AssetCreate, AssetResponse, AssetUpdate) from app/schemas/asset and emits a DeprecationWarning. – Tracks user behavior statistics for the AI risk scoring feature store. Functions: record_return() (increments total_returns, classifies on-time vs late by comparing return date to requested_end), record_damage() / record_lost() (increments respective counters), record_fine_issued() / record_fine_paid() (updates total_fines and unpaid_fines). All functions use _get_or_create_stats() to ensure the UserBehaviorStats row exists.

– Sequential code generation for all entities using the pattern PREFIX-YYYY-NNNN. Functions: generate_request_code(), generate_incident_code(), generate_invoice_code(), generate_transaction_code(). Queries the database for the latest code of each type and auto-increments.
The frontend is built with React 19 using functional components and hooks. Key architectural components:

– Root component implementing React Router DOM v7 with lazy-loaded, role-gated routes. Uses Suspense with a spinner fallback. Routes: / → /login, /user/* (role: user), /admin/* (role: admin), /manager/* (role: manager), /finance/* (role: finance).

– React Context-based authentication state management. Persists JWT and user profile in localStorage. Features: automatic token expiry detection by decoding JWT payload (base64), periodic expiry check every 60 seconds, login()/logout() functions. Exposes: isAuth, accessToken, user, userRole, userId, userName, userEmail.
– Route guard component. Checks isAuth (redirects to /login if false) and validates userRole against allowedRoles prop (redirects to user's own dashboard if role mismatch).

– Shared layout component used by all 4 role dashboards. Renders: sidebar with role title, navigation menu items with optional badges, user profile card, logout button. Main area: dynamic header with page title/subtitle, scrollable content area.

– Fetch wrapper that auto-attaches Authorization: Bearer <token> header. On HTTP 401/403, clears localStorage and dispatches auth-expired custom event. Exports: apiGet, apiPost, apiPut, apiPatch, apiDelete.
– Login service using OAuth2 form-encoded POST to /api/v1/auth/login. Returns { accessToken, tokenType, user }. Also provides getCurrentUser() and validateSession() helpers.
The database is implemented on Supabase (PostgreSQL 15) with Row Level Security (RLS) enabled on all tables. The schema is managed through SQL migration files in the server/migrations/ directory.
creates all 8 tables with the following key design decisions:
The users table uses uuid_generate_v4() for globally unique, non-sequential identifiers
The transactions table has a database trigger that prevents UPDATE and DELETE operations, enforcing immutability for audit integrity
RLS is enabled on all tables via ALTER TABLE ... ENABLE ROW LEVEL SECURITY for each table
transactions.previous_hash and current_hash columns (VARCHAR 64) support SHA-256 hash chaining for tamper detection
Foreign keys use ON DELETE RESTRICT (prevent deletion of referenced records) or ON DELETE CASCADE (handover_tokens cascade with requests)
All tables use server_default=func.now() for created_at and onupdate=func.now() for updated_at

populates the database with test data: 6 users (1 admin, 1 manager, 1 finance, 3 users with Low/Medium/High risk tiers), 6 assets (laptops, monitors, servers), 1 approved request with genesis handover transaction, 1 invoice, and 1 incident.

The frontend is implemented as a Single Page Application (SPA) using React 19, Vite 8 (build tool), and Tailwind CSS 4 for styling. All styles use Tailwind utility classes inline – no separate CSS files exist beyond the single @import "tailwindcss" entry.
The UI implements 4 role-based dashboards, each with a shared DashboardLayout component:

Dashboard (overview stats, recent activities, system alerts), Assets (device inventory with CRUD), Handover (pending handover list with confirm action), Users (user management with CRUD), Reports (return evaluation table)
Dashboard (CTA cards for request/incident), Assets (borrowed assets list), Requests (request history with risk level badges + NewRequestModal), Incidents (incident history + ReportIncidentModal)
Dashboard (metrics: pending approvals, active assets, incidents), Approvals (approve/reject high-risk requests), Risk Assessment (AI decision log with scores), Reports (executive report generation)
Dashboard (collected fines, pending invoices, unpaid fines), Fines (fine management with mark-as-paid), Invoices (invoice list), Payments (payment log), Reports (financial reports)

As of the current development phase, the frontend dashboard pages operate using static mockup data via React useState hooks. The backend API integration infrastructure is fully in place — apiClient.js provides a complete fetch wrapper with automatic JWT injection, and authService.js handles the login flow end-to-end. The remaining work involves wiring individual page components to their corresponding backend endpoints for live data fetching, which is planned for the next development iteration.

This project is a fully software-based, cloud-native web application. No hardware components or IoT devices are involved. The system runs entirely on cloud infrastructure (Supabase for database, Render for backend hosting, Vercel for frontend hosting).
The system integrates all modules through a RESTful API architecture:

The React frontend communicates with the FastAPI backend via the apiClient.js fetch wrapper. All requests include JWT Bearer tokens for authentication. The login flow uses OAuth2 form-encoded POST and stores the returned token in localStorage.

Every protected endpoint uses FastAPI dependency injection. The get_current_user dependency validates the JWT token, and require_role() enforces role-based access control. This ensures that, for example, only admin users can create/modify assets, and only finance users can verify payment proofs.

When a user creates a new asset request via POST /api/v1/asset-requests, the system snapshots the user's current risk_score and risk_score_tier from the User model. Based on the tier: High/Critical requests route to pending_manager for manual review, while Low/Medium requests route to pending_admin for standard approval.

As of the current implementation, the risk routing mechanism utilizes the user's existing risk_score and risk_score_tier values stored in the User model. The UserBehaviorStats table is actively being populated by behavior_service.py on every return, damage, lost, and fine event — serving as the denormalized feature store designed to feed the planned Random Forest classifier. The ML model training pipeline (using scikit-learn) and real-time inference integration into the request creation endpoint are scheduled for the next development phase.

When an admin generates a handover token (POST /handover-tokens/generate), the system creates a Transaction record with action=handover. When the user scans the token (POST /scan), the token status changes to used and the request status updates to handed_over.

The cryptographic integrity layer for the transaction ledger has been structurally implemented — the previous_hash and current_hash columns (VARCHAR 64) exist on the transactions table, and the database trigger enforces append-only immutability by preventing UPDATE and DELETE operations. Similarly, the handover_tokens table includes token and signature fields for Ed25519 digital signatures. As of the current phase, the SHA-256 hash computation and Ed25519 signing logic use temporary placeholder values. The full cryptographic implementation — including hash chain verification via GET /verify/ledger and Ed25519 key-pair generation per user — is designated for the cybersecurity-focused team member and is planned for integration in the subsequent development cycle.

When an admin processes a return via PATCH /asset-requests/{id}/return with a damaged or lost condition, the system automatically: (1) creates a Transaction record, (2) calculates the fine (purchase_value × 2 for damage/lost, Rp 50,000/day for late returns), (3) generates an Invoice with status unpaid, and (4) updates UserBehaviorStats via behavior_service.

The login page serves as the single entry point for all user roles. It features a clean, centered card design with the AFH branding logo, email and password input fields, a submit button with loading state, and an error message display area for invalid credentials. Upon successful login, users are automatically redirected to their role-specific dashboard (e.g., /admin for admin, /user for user). The page also handles JWT token storage and session initialization.
